newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MCGRATH AND HIS KNEES ON TRIAL AT WEST HAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MCGRATH AND HIS KNEES ON TRIAL AT WEST HAM.

text.p: Paul McGrath starts a three-match trial at West Ham this week in a bid to earn himself a one-year contract with the London side.

The 37-year-old centreback who has 82 Ireland caps -- and the most famous knees in English soccer -- must prove his fitness against Clyde, Dunfermline and St Johnstone after being released by Derby at the end of last season.

West Ham manager Harry Redknapp sees McGrath as the ideal man to help his side through their pre-season injury crisis. McGrath's troublesome knees would have meant retirement for many lesser players many years ago, but he has overcome a series of injuries and operations on them.
The highly-rated former Manchester United, Aston Villa and Derby player, could extend his already glittering career even longer as West Ham have serious deficiencies at the back.
Central defender Richard Hall will be out for several months following another operation on his troublesome foot, while skipper Julian Dicks also misses the start of the season after knee surgery.
With full-back Tim Breaker also due to enter hospital for teatment and Croatian Slaven Bilic having moved to Everton, McGrath was quick to answer Redknapp's distress call.
He said: "Harry very kindly invited me down to train with the team and get a bit of fitness.

With the situation he's in with defenders, he wants me around while he sees whether others are going to be getting fit. If they do, so be it. My attitude is at least I'm training. It's keeping me busy so I'm grateful to Harry for asking me here."

"I'll still be looking for a club to play for even if it's not West Ham," he insisted. "I'd love it to be West Ham because they're a premier league club and they've got a great pedigree of playing good football.

But I'm under no illusions that I'll be signing here just because I'm training with the boys. I look at some of the players they have at the club now and I think they could be in for a hell of a season."
Redknapp admitted he was surprised that a player of McGrath's class had been released by Derby.
He said: "It's his age I suppose. Paul's been a fantastic player. He did a great job for Derby last year. We played against them and he never gave us a kick in both games.
"He's still fit, also a good pro. He's coming to Scotland with us next week, so it will provide a good opportunity for us to have a look at him. We'll have a chat together and come to a decision."
